transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just standard paperwork and missed payments. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. Which is really frustrating because I bust my back at that store. I'm a supervisor, and just Tuesday I had to completely redo the front endcap displays because the new girl—I think her name is Brittany—put all the clearance items right at the main entrance. You don't put clearance at the front, you put the full-price seasonal items there to catch the foot traffic. I’ve been telling them this for months. I even drew a diagram for the breakroom wall. 

But anyway, it’s just like how no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years with this whole house situation. They really think I don't notice what they're doing. I actually wanted to paint the house yellow before all this started. Yellow is supposed to be a very calming color, don't you think? My grandmother had a yellow kitchen... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, they're all trying to force me out of my home.
Do you ever hear voices or see things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

No, I don't hear voices or anything like that. I mean, my hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, it's better than fine. Just the other day at work, I could hear the exact moment the receipt printer ran out of paper at register four, and I was all the way over in the stockroom. Which is ridiculous because Brittany was standing right there and didn't even notice. She just kept trying to ring up this woman who was buying, like, fifteen of those scented candles we just got in. The vanilla ones. I can't stand vanilla, it gives me a headache. I prefer citrus scents. I actually have a lemon tree in my backyard, well, the backyard of the house they're trying to take from me. It finally produced lemons this year. But no, I don't see or hear things that aren't there. I just see what they're doing with my house.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your ability to take care of your daily responsibilities, like bathing, cooking, or managing your work tasks, over the past six months?

No, I mean, I still get up every day. I have to. I supervise my team, I handle the schedules, I deal with all the customer issues. Like just yesterday, this guy was screaming at me over an expired coupon for dog food. It was for the huge bags of Pedigree. I don't even own a big dog, I have a little terrier mix named Buster. He has a very sensitive stomach, so I actually cook for him a lot. Just plain boiled chicken and rice, maybe some sweet potato. Sweet potatoes are on sale this week, actually, on endcap four. 

But yeah, I still cook for myself, I shower every morning—I use this eucalyptus body wash, it really wakes you up. It clears your sinuses right out. So my routine is perfectly fine. The only time things get... difficult, or I get thrown off track, is when the bank calls, or I get certain mail, or I see paperwork at work that I know is tied into what they're doing with my house. Because then I have to stop and document it. I have a whole system for tracking it now. I bought these color-coded folders from the stationery aisle. The blue ones are for the bank, the red ones are for the loan servicer... wait, did you ask about my schedule? But yeah, as long as the foreclosure stuff isn't actively being pushed in my face, I'm perfectly fine taking care of my normal responsibilities.
Have you ever shown the documents you have collected to someone you trust, like a friend or family member, to see if they agree with your interpretation of what the bank and your coworkers are doing?

No, I haven't really... I haven't shown them to anyone. I mean, I thought about showing my sister, Chloe. But she lives all the way out in Arizona now. She moved there like four years ago because her husband got transferred for his job. He works in HVAC, which is a really good industry to be in out there, obviously, with the heat. She always tells me it's a dry heat, but honestly, a hundred and ten degrees is a hundred and ten degrees. I went to visit her once in July and I swear my sandals started melting to the pavement. I actually had to go into a pharmacy and buy these special gel insoles just to walk around comfortably. 

They were the cooling gel kind, you know? The bright blue gel. Which actually is the exact same shade of blue as the folders I use for the bank documents. I like everything to be color-coordinated. It just makes things so much easier to track. Like at the store, I always make sure the seasonal displays have a cohesive color palette, otherwise the customers just walk right past it because it looks cluttered. Clutter really stresses people out, even if they don't realize it. But anyway, no, to answer your question, I haven't really let anyone else look through my paperwork.
When you are talking to others, do they ever tell you that they have trouble following what you are saying or that your thoughts seem to jump around?

No, people don't really say that to me. I mean, I communicate very clearly. You have to in retail, or nothing gets done right. Like, if I tell someone to restock the dairy case, I don't just say 'restock dairy.' I say, 'pull the older dates to the front and put the new ones in the back.' It's called FIFO—first in, first out. It's basic inventory management, but you'd be surprised how many people just shove the new milk right in the front. And then the old milk goes bad, and who has to deal with the smell? Me. It smells awful, like... sour yogurt, but worse. I actually used to make my own yogurt at home. I bought this little machine for it, you just put the milk in and let it sit. It was a fun hobby, but honestly, it took up too much counter space. My kitchen isn't that big. It's a nice kitchen, though, with these really pretty oak cabinets that I refinished myself a few years ago. Sanded them all down by hand. It took forever, my arms were so sore I could barely lift my coffee mug for a week. I drink a lot of coffee, usually dark roast. But anyway, no, nobody tells me I'm hard to follow. I think I'm pretty straightforward.
I noticed you enjoy talking about your hobbies and work, but can you tell me specifically why you decided to start keeping these color-coded folders for the bank documents?

Well, I started keeping the folders because... I mean, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just normal paperwork, you know? Like it's just missed payments or whatever. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been seeing it happen for almost two years now. And no amount of papers they try to show me changes what I know is really going on. That's why I need the folders. The blue ones, the red ones... I actually had to go to three different stores just to find the right shade of red. It's like a cherry red, not that weird maroon color. Maroon always reminds me of my high school marching band uniform. We had these awful wool uniforms, and it was so hot during the late summer games. I played the clarinet. I wasn't very good, honestly, I mostly just faked it during the really fast parts. The sheet music was always so tiny, I probably needed glasses even back then. I wear contacts now, the daily disposable ones. They're so much better than the ones you have to clean every night. The cleaning solution always made my eyes sting. But yeah, the folders are just to keep track of everything they're trying to do to my house.
When you are organizing your thoughts or explaining your system to others, do you ever feel like you have trouble keeping your focus on the main point without getting distracted by other details?

No, I don't think I get distracted. I mean, I stay focused on what matters, especially with the house and everything they're doing. It's just that all the details are connected, you know? You have to look at the whole picture. Like when I'm setting up a display at the store, you can't just look at one shirt. You have to look at the lighting, the signage, the way the mannequins are positioned. We got these new mannequins last month and they are so heavy. The old ones were fiberglass, I think, but these feel like solid concrete. I nearly dropped one on my foot trying to dress it in this new spring collection we got in. The spring collection is mostly pastels this year, which I'm not a huge fan of. I prefer jewel tones. Emerald green is my absolute favorite. I actually painted my bedroom emerald green right after I bought the house. It took three coats to get it even. I used that painter's tape, the blue kind, to keep the edges sharp around the ceiling. But yeah, I don't have trouble focusing. I just like to make sure I explain everything fully so people understand.

When you are explaining your system to me, do you realize that we often end up talking about things like your kitchen cabinets, your high school band, or your store displays instead of the bank documents?

I mean... I guess I bring those things up, but it's all part of the same thing. It's just how I talk, I guess. I'm just trying to give you the context. You need context, right? Like, you can't just jump into the middle of a story. It's like trying to watch a movie when you walk in halfway through. I did that once with my sister, we went to see that big superhero movie that came out a few years ago, but we missed the first twenty minutes because we were stuck in traffic. There was this huge accident on the interstate, a semi-truck tipped over and spilled all these boxes everywhere. It looked like they were full of paper towels or something. Which, honestly, is a mess, but at least it wasn't something hazardous. I hate driving on the interstate anyway, people drive way too fast. I always stick to the right lane. My car is getting kind of old, it's a 2012 sedan, and it vibrates a little if I go over sixty-five. I really need to get the tires rotated. The mechanic told me last time I was in for an oil change, but I just didn't have the time to wait around. The waiting room there is so depressing, just old magazines and bad coffee. But anyway, no, I don't think I'm avoiding the bank stuff. I'm just explaining things the way they happened.
Do you find that you have lost your spark or interest in the hobbies and activities you used to enjoy, like refinishing furniture or making yogurt, over the past few months?

No, I don't think I've lost interest. I mean, I still make my yogurt every week. Actually, I just made a big batch on Tuesday because I found this really good local whole milk at the farmer's market. You really have to use whole milk, the skim stuff just makes it super runny and sad. I tried it once with almond milk and it was a complete disaster, it totally separated in the glass jars. Almonds take so much water to grow anyway, I was reading this magazine article at the dentist's office about how they're draining all the water in California. I've never been to California, but I've always wanted to see the redwoods. The trees around my house are mostly just oaks and maples. There's this huge oak right in my front yard and the leaves are an absolute nightmare in the fall. I have to rake them like three times a week or they completely smother the grass. My neighbor uses one of those gas-powered leaf blowers, which is just so incredibly loud, especially on a Sunday morning when you're just trying to sit on the porch and drink your coffee. I prefer a French press for my coffee, by the way. It just tastes so much richer than a regular drip machine. But yeah, no, I still enjoy doing all my usual stuff, I haven't lost my spark for any of it.
